question: An otherwise eligible family moves permanently from another Canadian province to Alberta on May 18, registers promptly for AHCIP, and has no special exemption. When does Alberta coverage ordinarily start, and what should the family do during the waiting period?
generated_answer:
The family's Alberta coverage ordinarily starts on the first day of the third month following the month of registration. During the waiting period, the family should seek coverage from their former province of residence. 3.3 Coverage During Temporary Absences in Canada

3.3.1 Requirements

The Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan provides out-of-province health coverage to eligible Albertans who are temporarily absent from Alberta. The Alberta Health Care Insurance Act defines temporary absence as a period of time during which an insured person is absent from Alberta for the purpose of vacation or business. The Act also provides that an insured person is not considered to be temporarily absent from Alberta if the person stays outside Alberta for more than six months in a calendar year. 3.3.2 Exemptions

Alberta has entered into formal agreements with the Yukon Territory, the Northwest Territories, Nunavut, and Quebec to provide health care coverage to eligible residents of these jurisdictions who are temporarily in Alberta. Alberta also has a verbal agreement with British Columbia to provide health care coverage to eligible residents of British Columbia who are temporarily in Alberta. 3.3.3 Premiums

There are no premiums payable under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan. 3.3.4 Grievances and Appeals

An insured person who is not satisfied with a health care related decision regarding the person may make a request in writing to the Minister of Health and Wellness for a review of that decision. The Minister will then appoint a person to conduct an investigation and provide a report to the Minister. The Minister will then make a decision based on the report and provide a written response to the insured person. If the insured person is not satisfied with the Minister's decision, the person may appeal the decision to the Alberta Health Appeal Board. The Appeal Board is an independent administrative body that reports to the Legislative Assembly of Alberta through the Minister of Health and Wellness. The Appeal Board has the authority to confirm, vary, or reverse the Minister's decision. 3.4 Portability of Coverage During Temporary Absences Outside Canada
